about: The hero's company row (UI-5; Darko 2026-11-28: each company's own mark in its own colour, larger than its name, no card). A company is drawn with its mark only where it publishes that mark for this use and the use keeps its rules; otherwise it is its name in plain text (`text` says why: Wright's authorised fallback, 2026-11-28). Read 2026-11-28. Today every company is text.

row.name: ChatGPT
row.text: OpenAI publishes the Blossom (https://openai.com/brand/) under its marks terms, whose guidelines say "DON'T use the Blossom over a busy image" and prescribe its clear space; this row sits on the hero's detailed town photograph.

row.name: Claude
row.text: Anthropic's trademark guidelines (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/trademark-guidelines): "You may only use our trademarks as specifically permitted by us and only in materials we approve beforehand."

row.name: Gemini
row.text: Google's Partner Marketing Hub: a product icon needs an account and its approval form; for "works with" it says "Use plain text".

row.name: Meta AI
row.text: Meta publishes no Meta AI brand guidelines or asset (https://www.meta.com/brand/resources/), and "You may only use our trademarks with our permission".

row.name: Dearest
row.text: Dearest publishes no brand or press assets (dearest.app /press, /brand, /media are 404); its site icon is not a published reusable mark, and its terms' silence is not permission.

row.name: Nomi
row.text: Nomi publishes no brand or press assets; its terms (https://nomi.ai/terms-of-service/) say "Our logos displayed on the Site or the Service are our trademarks" and grant no use of them.

row.name: Letta
row.text: Letta publishes no brand or press assets, and its terms (https://www.letta.com/terms-of-service/) grant no right or licence to reproduce or use its marks.
